
'''Ōkunitama Shrine / Ōkunitama Shrine''' (おおくにたまじんじゃ) is the name used for certain Shinto shrines, rendered either as "大国魂神社" or "大國魂神社", and also sometimes written as "大国霊神社" or "大国玉神社". Below is an explanation of the differences in the kanji spellings followed by a list of the major shrines under each spelling.

== Spelled as "大国魂神社" ==
This form uses the simplified character [[Country|国]] in place of the traditional [[Country]]. It is the form commonly used in modern contexts.
* [[Aizu Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Fukushima Prefecture]], [[Ōnuma District]], [[Aizumisato]], Miyabayashi: a subsidiary shrine within the precincts of [[Isasumi Shrine]].
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine (Sakai City, Sakai Ward)]] – located in [[Osaka Prefecture]], [[Sakai|Sakai City]], [[Sakai-ku, Sakai|Sakai Ward]], [[Q131912534]]: a subsidiary shrine within the precincts of [[Aguchi Shrine]].

=== Branches of [[Ōyamato Shrine]] ===
* [[Yamato Okunitama Shrine, Minamiawaji]] – located in [[Hyōgo Prefecture]], [[Minamiawaji|Minamiawaji City]], Enokiretsu.
* [[Yamato Okunitama Shrine, Mima]] – located in [[Tokushima Prefecture]], [[Mima, Tokushima|Mima City]], [[Mimachō]], Shigekiyo.

== Spelled as "大國魂神社" ==
This form retains the traditional character [[Country]] and is often used by shrines that emphasize historical prestige or formality.
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine (Iwaki)]] – located in [[Fukushima Prefecture]], [[Iwaki, Fukushima|Iwaki City]], Hirasuganami.
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Tokyo|Tokyo Metropolis]], [[Fuchū, Tokyo|Fuchū City]], [[Miyamachi]]: the head shrine (総社) of [[Musashi Province]], hosting the annual grand festival [[Kurayami Matsuri]].
* [[Shima Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Nagasaki Prefecture]], [[Tsushima, Nagasaki|Tsushima City]], Kamitsushima Town.

== Spelled as "大国霊神社" ==
This variant uses the character [[Soul]] (rei) instead of [[Soul]] (tama). The reading may be "Ōkunitama Jinja" or "Ōkunirei Jinja".
* [[Owari Ōkunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Inazawa|Inazawa City]], [[Kōnomiya]]: also known as Kokufumiya Shrine.

== Spelled as "大国玉神社" ==
This variant employs the character [[Q11572333]] (tama) to denote sacred treasures. It is usually rendered in the simplified form "大国玉神社", though in some cases the traditional form "大國玉神社" is used.
* [[Okunitama Shrine]] – located in [[Ibaraki Prefecture]], [[Sakuragawa, Ibaraki|Sakuragawa City]], Ogunitama: also referred to as 大國玉神社.
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine (Matsusaka)]] – located in [[Mie Prefecture]], [[Matsusaka|Matsusaka City]], Rokkon Town.
* [[Ōkunitama Shrine (Iki)]] – located in [[Nagasaki Prefecture]], [[Iki, Nagasaki|Iki City]], Gounoura Town.
